title.en: Rotational symmetry and symmetry in numbers

text.en: Lali makes a windmill (firki). When she turns it a quarter, a half, three-quarters or a full turn, it looks exactly the same! This is another kind of symmetry - rotational symmetry.

A shape has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after turning less than a full turn about its centre.
A firki looks the same after 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 turn, and of course after a full turn. A dot on it helps us track the turn.
The letter H looks the same after a half turn. So H has rotational symmetry. A also has reflection symmetry, but turned halfway it does not look like A, so it has no rotational symmetry.
Check letters by cutting them out, fixing the centre with a pin and turning, or by tracing paper. Letters like N, S, X, O and H have rotational symmetry.
Digits: 0, 1, 3, 8 have reflection symmetry. 0 and 8 have rotational symmetry too (1 if written as a plain straight stroke). So 0 and 8 have both.
Numbers: 11 and 1001 look the same after a half turn and also have a vertical line, so they have both symmetries. 69 and 96 look the same after a half turn. 88 and 808 have both.
Try making your own 2-, 3-, 4-digit numbers: 88, 808, 8008 or 69 - check each by turning the page upside down.

problem.en: Does the number 69 have rotational symmetry?

why.en: A half turn flips the page upside down.

text.en: 6 becomes 9 and 9 becomes 6, in swapped places, so it reads 69 again. Yes, 69 has rotational symmetry.

why.en: The look is the same after a half turn.

prompt.en: Tell a friend how to test if a shape has rotational symmetry.

requiredIdeas.en: Mark a dot and fix the centre with a pin
If it looks the same before a full turn, it has rotational symmetry

commonMisconceptions.en: Confusing it with folding for reflection symmetry

points.en: Rotational symmetry: looks the same after turning less than a full turn.
Firki: 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 turns. H: half turn.
Digits 0 and 8 have both reflection and rotational symmetry.
Numbers like 69, 88, 808 and 1001 have rotational symmetry.
